text:
kevin: thinking about a safer 'spillover' burst backstop for mixed pools — want to keep a small always-on on-demand floor (hard floor) + opportunistic spot burst that has graceful handoff when interruptions happen. TL;DR: min_on_demand_percent + preemptible drain window + local fallback lanes. Thoughts? :thinking:

maria: love the idea. can we define SLOs that map to floor size? e.g., 99th latency vs cost.

ravi: agree. one gotcha — regions with few capacity types can force bigger on-demand floors. we should allow region overrides.

olivia: proposed config sketch:
```
min_on_demand_percent: 15
burst_pool: {
  max_burst_ratio: 3.0
  preemptible_drain_seconds: 120
  eviction_credit_bucket: 500
}
fallback_policy: ["local-on-demand", "cross-region-on-demand", "serve-reject"]
```

aj: nit: make drain window adaptive: longer for long-running KV-cache warmups. also telemetry hooks for interruption reason.

kevin: good point. also think we need a 'spillover token' concept — tokens consumed when spot is used; replenish when on-demand freed. keeps fairness.

infra-bot: deploy queued: mixpool/experimental/spillover-v1 -> staging

maria: tests we need: 1) spot-drain during steady surge 2) region-restricted fleet + burst 3) latency 99th under 1s. I'll add to test plan.

ravi: cost modeling — simulate 30/70 spot/on-demand with 10% interruptions -> expected savings ~35% vs all on-demand if preemption handling is good.

olivia: question: when fallback cross-region, must ensure data locality for private deployments. add a constraint flag `allow_cross_region_fallback` per tenant.

kevin: action items:
- @maria add SLO->floor mapping doc
- @aj add adaptive drain prototype
- @olivia add tenant flag and k8s operator changes
- @ravi run cost sim for ap-southeast vs us-west
I'll follow up with a short design doc link: https://go/internal/mixpool-spillover

maria: ack :thumbsup:

aj: will PR drain logic this week

kevin: thanks everyone. if no objections, we can run canary on staging next Tue :rocket:
